content.summary: Guidance on management of aortic and mitral valve disease in patients with heart failure (HF), including indications for intervention, medical therapy considerations, and Heart Team decision-making.

aortic_regurgitation_12.3.2.clinical_summary: Severe aortic regurgitation (AR) can cause progressive left ventricular (LV) dilation, dysfunction, HF and poor prognosis. Medical therapy (MT) can improve symptoms; RAAS inhibitors may be useful. Beta-blockers should be used cautiously as they prolong diastole and may worsen AR. Aortic valve surgery is recommended for patients with severe AR and HF symptoms regardless of LVEF. In patients at high or prohibitive surgical risk, TAVI has been used to treat AR.
recommendations: Consider RAAS inhibitors for symptom improvement in severe AR.
Use beta-blockers cautiously in AR due to potential worsening of regurgitation.
Aortic valve surgery recommended for severe AR with HF symptoms regardless of LVEF.
Consider TAVI in high or prohibitive surgical risk patients to treat AR.

primary_organic_mitral_regurgitation.clinical_summary: Primary (organic) MR is caused by valve apparatus abnormalities and can lead to HF. Surgery, preferably repair, is recommended for patients with severe primary MR and HF symptoms. If surgery is contraindicated or high risk, percutaneous repair may be considered.
recommendations: Prefer mitral valve repair for severe primary MR with HF symptoms.
If surgery contraindicated or high surgical risk, consider percutaneous mitral repair.

secondary_functional_mitral_regurgitatio.clinical_summary: Secondary MR (SMR) is mainly a disease of the left ventricle and can be caused by mitral annulus enlargement due to LA dilation. Moderate or severe SMR in patients with HF is associated with very poor prognosis. Assessment of MR aetiology and severity should be done by an experienced echocardiographer using a multiparametric approach, ideally in stable patient conditions after optimization of medical and resynchronization therapies.
assessment_and_management_points: SMR assessment requires multiparametric echocardiographic evaluation by experienced operators after optimization of medical and device therapy.
Exercise echocardiography/echocardiographic quantification during exercise may help in patients with moderate SMR at rest and symptoms during activity.
Early referral of HF patients with moderate or severe MR to a multidisciplinary Heart Team (including HF specialists) is recommended for assessment and treatment planning.
The Heart Team must first verify the patient is on optimal therapy, including CRT when indicated.
In patients with severe SMR and HFrEF requiring revascularisation, mitral valve surgery and CABG should be considered.
Isolated mitral valve surgery may be considered in symptomatic patients with severe SMR despite optimal therapy (text truncated on page).

procedural_considerations_and_heart_team.clinical_summary: Choice between TAVI and SAVR should be decided by the Heart Team considering age, life expectancy, patient preference and anatomical/clinical features. Colour coding for classes of recommendation referenced. Balloon aortic valvuloplasty may be considered as a bridge in highly symptomatic patients with acute HF or cardiogenic shock or as bridge to TAVI/SAVR, or in advanced HF as BTR or DT.
